classification.difficultyReason: The obtuse largest angle by the cosine rule, then the smallest by the sine rule: the same structure as the reference.

content.prompt: Consider the triangle shown. Answer to the nearest degree.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Use cosine rule to find the size of the largest angle.

answer.worked:
The largest angle $A$ is opposite side $14$.
$$\begin{align*}\cos A&=\frac{7^2+9^2-14^2}{2(7)(9)}\\[8pt]A&=\cos^{-1}\left(-\frac{11}{21}\right)\\[8pt]A&\approx122^\circ\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Use sine rule to find the size of the smallest angle.

answer.worked:
The smallest angle $B$ is opposite side $7$. Use the unrounded value of $A$ from part a.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{\sin B}{7}&=\frac{\sin A}{14}\\[8pt]B&=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{7\sin A}{14}\right)\\[8pt]B&\approx25^\circ\end{align*}$$
